No new retrieval occurred during Revision 1. No source field, reference,
passage locator, direct quotation, experiment, code result, proof
result, or canonical manuscript byte was introduced. The Phase-6
ClaimIntent manifest records eight claims frozen before the Revision-1
prose; it is a historical inventory, not an exhaustive inventory of the
claims in the current manuscript. Every finding below is
either a closed-corpus evidence-synthesis statement, a project
definition, or a prospective method obligation.

The new wording makes the expansion prospective and limits it to byte/bookkeeping regression. Explicit exclusion of self, ordered-reversal, and triple fixtures and of independently expected semantic labels agrees with B0061/B0062. No comparative-superiority, executed-test, owner count, or semantic-oracle claim is added.

evidence.scope: Inherited population accounting only; no P31 owner-canonicalization replay.
Unchanged controlling declared pair/fixture coverage and absent independent semantic route.

arithmetic.meaning: Number of unordered distinct-input pairs, not owners or performed tests.

changed_block_review.reviewed_current_text:
Pair rows can also test equivalence-relation consequences globally. A
same-owner relation derived from canonical bytes is automatically
reflexive, symmetric, and transitive at the byte level, but producer or
serialization defects may still appear as inconsistent input bindings,
inverse labels, or traversal metadata. The proposed 9,453-row expansion covers all unordered distinct-input
pairs as a byte and bookkeeping regression audit, not as the primary
proof object. It includes no self, ordered-reversal, or triple fixtures
and supplies no independent expected semantic labels.

changed_block_review.reason: The amended I_diag-only referent and refusal to report any of G, I, or C as complete when an input remains unresolved match the controlling B0067 and B0113 schema: X_res=X is the materialization gate for all three estimands, while I_diag has no projection into complete estimands. The edit preserves the original fail-closed rule and adds no materialized relation or owner count.

evidence.scope: Controlling relation definitions and total-disposition/materialization gate.
The pre-existing distinct-estimand and zero-unresolved intent.

changed_block_review.reviewed_current_text:
Materialization must remain conditional on zero unresolved owner rows.
If even one input cannot be rooted or canonicalized, only \texttt{I\_diag}
may retain its unresolved diagnostic record, and \texttt{G}, \texttt{I},
and \texttt{C} cannot be reported as complete estimands. A partial table may be useful for method
development only if it is labeled incomplete and does not award owner
counts. This stop rule prevents missing inputs from being silently
treated as new, different, or irrelevant owners.

changed_block_review.reason: The replacement removes the unsupported most-demanding adversarial superlative. It retains the distinction between a canonical proof object and a proposed 9,453-row pair audit, explicitly denies omitted-fixture coverage and an independent semantic adjudicator, and remains compatible with B0061/B0062. It does not claim that an invariant has been implemented, a biconditional proved, or a fixture set executed.

evidence.scope: Prospective pair-audit scope and local old/new conclusion context.
Approved removal of unsupported comparative-superiority wording.

changed_block_review.reviewed_current_text:
The revised architecture improves the match between the mathematical
object and its evidence. A partition is naturally represented by a total
equivalence invariant. Expanding that invariant to every pair can be an
excellent audit, but expansion size should not be confused with proof
content. This distinction treats the 9,453 unordered distinct-pair rows as a
proposed byte and bookkeeping audit rather than a prerequisite proof
object, without claiming coverage of the omitted fixture shapes or an
independent semantic adjudicator.
